Headline: Free Burn Treatment Camp to Benefit Patients in Dhangadhi
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited, in collaboration with Sushma Koirala Memorial Hospital and Seti Provincial Hospital, is organizing a free burn treatment camp in Dhangadhi from Falgun 12 to 14. The initiative, conducted under the bank’s Corporate Social Responsibility program, aims to provide consultation, treatment, and surgeries to more than 120 burn survivors, especially those from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.
Patients suffering from contractures, fused fingers, mobility issues, and other burn-related complications will receive specialized care, while severe cases will be referred to Kathmandu for further treatment at no cost. The program seeks to address Nepal’s high number of burn incidents and improve access to timely medical care outside the capital, with plans to expand similar camps to other provinces in the future.

Headline: Nabil Bank Launches Modern Digital Lounge at Kamaladi
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has launched a modern Digital Lounge at Nabil House, Kamaladi, aiming to provide customers with fast, convenient, and technology-friendly banking services. The lounge was jointly inaugurated by Chairman Nirvana Chaudhary and Director Sarita Bhatta Adhikari in the presence of board members and senior management.
The facility enables customers to carry out 24/7 digital transactions, including cash withdrawals through ATMs, cash deposits via deposit machines, and digital cheque deposits through kiosks. The bank believes the multi-purpose digital setup will save customers’ time and enhance service efficiency.
Similar digital lounges are already in operation at the bank’s head office and in Itahari. With this expansion, Nabil Bank aims to reduce reliance on traditional counter services and strengthen its shift toward digital banking. Currently, the bank serves over 2.5 million customers through 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide, continuing its four-decade legacy while promoting sustainable and digital banking initiatives.

Headline: Falgun Interest Rate Update: Commercial Banks Revise Fixed Deposit Rates; Majority Keep Rates Unchanged
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published new interest rates for the month of Falgun, showing a decline compared to Poush.
Out of the 20 commercial banks currently in operation, 8 have reduced their rates, while the remaining 12 banks have continued with the same rates on individual fixed deposits as in the previous month.
Global IME Bank recorded the steepest reductions, each lowering the rates on individual fixed deposits by 0.75 percentage points.
Meanwhile Citizens Bank International , Himalayan Bank, kumari Bank, Laxmi Sunrise Bank, Maccha puchre Bank, Nabil Bank, Nepal Bank, NIC Asia Bank, NMB Bank, Prabhu Bank, Rastriya Banjiya Bank and Sanima Bank have maintained the same rates as in Poush.

Headline: Nabil Bank Earns Rs. 4.76 Arba Net Profit with EPS of Rs. 35.04 in Q2 FY 2082/83
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL)
reported a net profit of Rs. 4.76 arba in the second quarter of FY 2082/83, marking a notable improvement compared to Rs. 3.27 arba in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year.
The bank’s net interest income increased to Rs. 8.08 arba, up from Rs. 7.89 arba in Q2 FY 2081/82, reflecting growth in its core banking operations. Total deposits stood at Rs. 5.66 Kharba, while loans and advances expanded to Rs. 4.34 Kharba during the review period.
Operating profit surged to Rs. 6.57 arba, supported mainly by a reversal in impairment charges, which stood at negative Rs. 4.88 crore, compared to impairment expenses of Rs. 1.35 arba in the same quarter last year. However, personnel expenses rose to Rs. 2.87 arba during the period.
The bank posted an earnings per share (EPS) of Rs. 35.04, while net worth per share reached Rs. 235.64. The capital adequacy ratio improved to 12.77 percent, and the cost of fund declined to 3.62 percent.
At the end of the quarter, Nabil Bank’s shares were trading at Rs. 487.50, with a price-earnings (PE) ratio of 13.91 times.

Headline: Nirvana Kumar Chaudhary Sworn in as Chairman of Nabil Bank
Full Content:
Nirvana Kumar Chaudhary has officially taken the oath as the new Chairman of Nabil Bank Limited, administered by Nepal Rastra Bank Governor Pro. Dr. Bishwanath Poudel. Chaudhary was elected as Chairman during the bank’s 699th Board Meeting held on Poush 28, 2082.
A prominent business leader, Chaudhary is Managing Director of Chaudhary Group and serves as Vice-Chairman of Chaudhary Foundation and Senior Vice-President of the Confederation of Nepalese Industries (CNI).
The oath-taking ceremony was attended by Nepal Rastra Bank officials, Nabil Bank directors, CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali, Deputy CEO Bhupendra Pandey, and other senior officials.
Nabil Bank operates 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide, serving over 25 lakh customers. The bank, with over 40 years of banking service, has embraced sustainable banking and expanded digital services through its nBank platform.

Headline: Nabil Bank Marks Fellowship Milestone Through Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has bid farewell to participants of the fourth and fifth cohorts and welcomed the sixth cohort of its fellowship program under the Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship (Nabil SSE). The event, titled “Celebrating Fellowship: Journey of Impact, 2082,” marked the certification of 40 fellows from the fourth and fifth groups and the induction of 20 new participants into the sixth cohort. The program, run under Nabil Bank’s corporate social responsibility in partnership with Tribhuvan University School of Management, focuses on promoting social entrepreneurship in Nepal.
Speaking at the event, bank officials and academic leaders highlighted the program’s role in encouraging youth to pursue entrepreneurship within the country, creating employment opportunities, and contributing to sustainable development. Since its launch in 2021, Nabil SSE has supported the establishment of numerous social enterprises, generating thousands of jobs nationwide. The fellowship provides practical, mentorship-based training and networking support, reinforcing Nabil Bank’s long-term commitment to inclusive growth and social impact through entrepreneurship.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Magh Interest Rates; HBL and  MBL Leads with Significant Cuts
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published new interest rates for the month of Magh, showing a decline compared to Poush.
Out of the 20 commercial banks currently in operation, 11 have reduced their rates, while the remaining banks have continued with the same rates on individual fixed deposits as in the previous month.
Himalayan Bank and Macchapuchre Bank recorded the steepest reductions, each lowering the rates on individual fixed deposits by 0.5 percentage points. Meanwhile Global Ime Bank, Nabil Bank, Nepal Investment Mega Bank, Nepal Bank, NIC Asia Bank, NMB Bank, Prabhu Bank, Rastriya Banjiya Bank and Prime Commercial Bank have maintained the same rates as in Poush.

Headline: Nabil Bank Approves 12.50% Cash Dividend, Elects New Chairman
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has approved a 12.50 percent cash dividend for its shareholders from the profit of fiscal year 2081/82 during its 41st Annual General Meeting held under the chairmanship of Upendra Prasad Paudel. The AGM also unanimously elected Anil Keshari Shah as a director representing the promoter shareholders.
Following this, the bank’s board selected Nirvana Kumar Chaudhary as the new Chairman, who will assume office after taking the oath from Nepal Rastra Bank.
Outgoing Chairman Paudel completed two terms, during which the bank achieved notable progress in sustainable banking, digital transformation, team building, social entrepreneurship initiatives, and merger management.
In the current fiscal year 2082/83, Nabil Bank has issued NPR 5 Arba worth of 8% irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares to strengthen its capital base and risk-bearing capacity, supporting further business expansion. The bank currently operates through 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide, serving over 2.5 million customers, and continues to promote digital and sustainable banking through its NBank platform.

Headline: Nabil Bank Honored as ‘Bikash Nayak 2082’ for Outstanding Contribution to Nepal’s Economic Growth
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has been awarded the prestigious ‘Bikash Nayak 2082’ honor by Bikash Media in recognition of its outstanding contribution to Nepal’s economic development. The award was presented to CEO Manoj Gyawali by Finance Minister Rameshwor Prasad Khanal in the presence of Chairman Upendra Prasad Paudel.
With over four decades of leadership in Nepal’s banking sector, Nabil Bank has played a key role in promoting financial inclusion, digital innovation, entrepreneurship, employment generation, and national revenue growth. The bank has been a pioneer in digital banking through platforms like the nBank app, expanding financial access across the country.
Nabil Bank is also a major contributor to energy and infrastructure development, having committed around NPR 75 billion to more than 3,100 MW of hydropower and renewable energy projects. It has been recognized eight times as the highest tax-paying bank in the financial sector.
Beyond banking, Nabil Bank actively supports social responsibility initiatives in education, health, disaster response, and financial literacy, helping generate over 17,000 jobs through social entrepreneurship programs. Today, it serves more than 2.5 million customers through 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide, maintaining its position as one of Nepal’s leading and most influential banks.

Headline: Khalti Wallet Users Can Now Withdraw Cash from Nabil Bank ATMs
Full Content:
Khalti wallet users can now withdraw cash from Nabil Bank ATMs without using a card, following a partnership between the two institutions. Users can withdraw up to NPR 5,000 daily and NPR 25,000 monthly.
To use the service, users enter the withdrawal amount in the Khalti app, receive an OTP, and complete the transaction at the ATM via the cardless withdrawal option. The service provides a convenient, secure way to access cash anytime, especially when a card is unavailable, enhancing digital financial access across Nepal.

Headline: Nabil Bank Wins Nepal’s Best Transaction Bank Award 2025
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has been awarded Nepal’s Best Transaction Bank Award 2025 under the Euromoney Transaction Banking Awards, recognizing its technology-driven, customer-centric transaction banking services. The award highlights the bank’s effective digital payment solutions for individual, institutional, and SME clients, which have made banking services more secure, efficient, and convenient.
Chief Executive Officer Manoj Kumar Gyawali stated that the recognition reflects the bank’s continuous efforts, commitment to innovation, and the trust of its customers. Euromoney Awards, established in 1992, are regarded as one of the most prestigious global honors in the banking and financial sector, operating across more than 100 countries.
Nabil Bank, one of Nepal’s leading banks, serves over 2.5 million customers through 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide. For more than four decades, the bank has played a pioneering role in introducing innovative banking services and contributing significantly to the development of Nepal’s banking sector.

Headline: Nabil Bank  Unveils Book Closure Date for its 12.50% Cash Dividend; Calls AGM on Poush 28
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL)
has called its 41st AGM on 28th Poush, 2082. The meeting will be held in the Tribhuwan Army Office, Bhadrakali, Kathmandu starting at 11:15 am that day.
Among the other agendas, the AGM will endorse a 12.50% cash dividend for the fiscal year 2081/82. The 694th board of directors meeting on Mangsir 19 decided to distribute the dividend on the paid-up capital of Rs. 27.05 Arba. A 12.50% cash dividend (for tax purposes) has been proposed. Thus, the cash dividend (including for tax purposes) is worth Rs. 3.38 Arba.
Furthermore, an agenda is to endorse the auditor's report with PL statements, financial reports, and cash flow reports, and appoint an auditor for the fiscal year 2082/83.
The book closure date is on Poush 16. Therefore, the shareholders who maintained before that day are entitled to dividend payout, and can attend this AGM.

Headline: Nabil Bank Allots Rs. 5 Arba Worth of 8% Irredeemable Non-Cumulative Preference Shares
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has completed the allotment of ‘Nabil 8% Perpetual Non-cumulative Preference Share’ worth Rs. 5 Arba. The bank issued 5 crores units of preference shares at a face value of Rs. 100 per share, following approval from the Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON).
The shares were allotted on Poush 1 through a private placement to institutional investors. This marks the first time SEBON has approved the issuance of irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares by a bank after relevant policy provisions were introduced by Nepal Rastra Bank and SEBON.
The issuance is expected to strengthen Nabil Bank’s capital base through additional Tier-1 capital, enhance risk-bearing capacity, and support future business expansion.

Headline: Nabil Bank Opens First Priority Banking Lounge Outside Kathmandu in Pokhara
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has launched its sixth Priority Banking Lounge at the Pokhara branch, marking the first such lounge outside the Kathmandu Valley. The lounge, inaugurated by Deputy CEO Adarsha Bajgain, aims to provide high-quality, personalized banking services.
Through Nabil Priority Banking, customers can access relationship managers, enjoy streamlined lounge services, and receive financial and investment advice. Nabil Bank, a leading bank in Nepal, serves over 2.5 million customers across 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide and has been at the forefront of innovative banking services for over four decades.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Poush Interest Rates; GBIME, PCBL and RBBL Leads with Significant Cuts
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published new interest rates for the month of Poush, showing a decline compared to Mangsir.
Out of the 20 commercial banks currently in operation, 13 have reduced their rates, while the remaining banks have continued with the same rates on individual fixed deposits as in the previous month.
Global IME Bank, Prime Commercial Bank and Rastriya Banijya Bank recorded the steepest reductions, each lowering the rates on individual fixed deposits by 0.5 percentage points. Meanwhile, Citizens Bank International, Siddhartha Bank, Machhapuchchhre Bank, Nepal Investment Mega Bank, NIC Asia Bank, NMB Bank, and Himalayan Bank have maintained the same rates as in Mangsir.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Kartik; GBIME Tops the Charts
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for the fourth month of the fiscal year 2082/83, ending in Kartik.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 19.37 Arba. Global IME Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 2.51 Arba, overtaking Nabil Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 2.46 Crores. Prime Commercial Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 1.58 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Everest Bank and NMB Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the Citizens Bank International recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 1.64 Crores.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 1.79 Arba, despite eight out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Garima Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 39.77 Crores, outpacing Garima Bikas Bank, Muktinath Bikas Bank, which posted Rs. 38.42 Crores in net profit. Shine Resunga Development Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 30.25 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Miteri Development Bank and Green Development Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 3.5 Crores and Rs. 2.18 Crores, respectively.
Furthermore, seven banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Corporate Development Bank, Sindhu Bikas Bank, Salapa, Lumbini Bikas Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: Nabil Bank and TU Renew Nabil SSE Program to Boost Social Entrepreneurship
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited and Tribhuvan University’s Faculty of Management have renewed their agreement to continue the ‘Nabil SSE’ social entrepreneurship program until 2028. The program, run under Nabil Bank’s CSR initiative for the past four years, supports social entrepreneurship through fellowship and certificate courses.
The fellowship offers six months of training and a year of mentorship, while the certificate course is conducted across all provinces. So far, 96 fellows have established 62 enterprises benefitting over 14,000 people, and 1,069 certificate graduates have created 131 enterprises generating more than 2,600 jobs. Both institutions stated that the renewed collaboration will strengthen entrepreneurship development, community impact, and practical education.

Full Content:

has proposed a 12.50% cash dividend for the fiscal year 2081/82.
The 694th meeting of the board of directors held on Mangsir 19, 2082, decided to distribute the dividend on the paid-up capital of Rs. 27.05 Arba. A 12.50% cash dividend (including tax) has been proposed.
The dividend will be distributed only after approval by the central bank and endorsement by the company's upcoming AGM. As of writing, NABIL has an LTP of Rs. 510.20.

Headline: Nabil Bank Expands International Payment Service to 27 Branches Nationwide
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has expanded its international payment service to 27 branches across Nepal. Previously available only at the central office and a few selected branches, the service will now be accessible at 17 branches within the Kathmandu Valley and 10 branches outside the valley. According to Deputy CEO Adarsha Bazgain, the expansion aims to strengthen the bank’s digital and international banking capabilities.
Through Nabil Online Payment Service, customers can make secure global payments, including visa application fees, university or college application fees, insurance, ACCA payments, and fees for educational or business conferences, without needing a separate international card.
Nabil Bank, one of Nepal’s leading banks, serves over 2.5 million customers through 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide and continues to play a pioneering role in introducing innovative banking services for over four decades.

Headline: Nabil Bank Wins Three Prestigious Visa International Awards
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has won three major awards from Visa International: Excellence in Consumer Debit Cards Business Principal Client, Excellence in Contactless, Issuing, and Excellence in E-Commerce Acquiring Business Principal Client. The awards were presented at an event held at the Marriott Hotel, Kathmandu.
Deputy CEO Adarsha Bazgain credited the achievement to the bank’s customers, businesses, and staff, noting it as a source of motivation. As one of Nepal’s leading banks, Nabil serves over 2.5 million customers through 268 branches and 321 ATMs, playing a pioneering role in advancing banking services and innovation in the country.

Headline: Lumbini Ceramics Partners with Nabil Bank for Dealer Channel Financing
Full Content:
Lumbini Ceramics Ltd., manufacturer of Laminar Tiles, has signed an agreement with Nabil Bank to provide channel financing facilities to its dealers across Nepal. The partnership, formalized by CFO Prakash Poudel and Nabil Bank’s Chief Business Officer, Tek Raj Bhatta, will help dealers access easier working capital and improve inventory management.
Nabil Bank will offer additional benefits such as reduced loan fees, discounts on LC and bank guarantees, 50% off corporate banking services, free SMS alerts, free credit cards for key dealer staff, and critical illness insurance. The collaboration aims to boost dealer liquidity, lower financial pressure, and support the growth of Nepal’s tiles sector.

Headline: Nabil Bank Partners with NiB-GA to Boost SME Growth Through £4.5 Million Grant Program
Full Content:
Nabil Bank and Nepal in Business – Growth Advisors (NiB-GA) have formed a strategic partnership to strengthen support for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) across Nepal. The agreement, signed by Nabil Bank CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali and NiB-GA Team Leader Ratish Basnyat, enables the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) to provide £4.5 million in grants to 40 SMEs within prioritized sectors and regions.
The initiative aims to help SMEs expand operations, enhance efficiency, and improve export readiness. CEO Gyawali highlighted that the program will uplift SME confidence and allow Nabil Bank to facilitate financing and SME-focused loans.
Basnyat appreciated Nabil Bank’s role in ensuring transparent grant management, noting that the model could be useful for similar future projects and even government-level capital expenditure.
As the financial partner, Nabil Bank will handle secure and efficient grant disbursement, ensuring accountability throughout the program. The NiB-GA Program, funded by UK International Development and implemented by DAI Global UK, focuses on enhancing SME productivity, competitiveness, and sustainable employment. Nabil Bank, a leading institution with 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide, continues to emphasize digital transformation and innovative financial services.

Headline: Nabil Bank's Rs. 5 Arba 'Nabil 8% Perpetual Non-cumulative Preference Share' Issue Approved by SEBON
Full Content:
The Securities Exchange Board of Nepal (SEBON) has provided the final approval to the proposed issue of
"Nabil 8% Perpetual Non-cumulative Preference Share"
in the latest list of debentures approved.
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) is seeking to raise a debt of Rs. 5 Arba through the total issue, with 5 crores units to be subscribed via private placement. The regulatory board gave the nod of approval on Mangsir 05, 2082.
The debentures will provide an 8% interest rate per annum.
NIC Asia Capital Limited has been appointed as the issue manager for the debenture issue.

Headline: Nabil Bank Expands Appointment Banking Service to 13 Branches in Kathmandu Valley
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has expanded its appointment banking service from its central office in Teendhara to 13 branches across Kathmandu Valley. The service aims to enhance efficiency, convenience, and digital service delivery, particularly benefiting busy professionals and customers with limited time.
CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali expressed confidence that the expansion will strengthen customer relationships and provide modern, hassle-free banking. Through this service, customers can conduct cash and cheque transactions quickly without waiting in line. Appointments can be booked via Nabil Bank’s website or nBank app. Nabil Bank currently serves over 2.5 million customers through 268 branches and 321 ATMs nationwide.

Headline: Nabil Bank Launches New Mastercard Debit Card with Exclusive Benefits
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has introduced a new debit card under the Mastercard network to enhance digital payment experiences and customer convenience. The launch event in Kathmandu was attended by senior officials from Nabil Bank and Mastercard. CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali highlighted that the card reflects the bank’s commitment to international-standard services, while Mastercard’s Ravi Datla emphasized secure and convenient payments.
The card offers access to Mastercard’s global network, a design featuring Nepal’s national bird, Danphe, and premium benefits like discounts at restaurants, spas, fitness centers, and entertainment venues. Customers can apply through Nabil Bank branches or the nBank app. With 268 branches and 321 ATMs, Nabil Bank continues to lead Nepal’s banking sector through innovation and digital transformation.

Headline: Unveiling Q1 FY 2082/83: A Comprehensive Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks and Key Financial Insights
Full Content:
All 20 commercial banks have unveiled their financial reports for the first quarter of FY 2082/83, offering a fresh look into their performance during the third-month period. The disclosures present a deeper understanding of their profitability, capital strength, and overall business growth. This summary captures the major highlights and evolving trends in net earnings, capital adequacy ratios, and other essential financial indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q1 FY 2082/83, Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led with a net profit of Rs. 1.86 Arba, marking a 22.88% increase over the same period last year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) followed with a net profit of Rs. 1.76 Arba, though this represents a 14.59 % decrease from the previous year. Prime Commercial Bank Limited (GBIME) took third with Rs. 1.26 Arba.

Headline: Nabil Bank’s Net Profit Declines by 14.57% to Rs. 1.75 Arba in Q1 FY 2082/83; Net Interest Income at Rs. 3.90 Arba

Nabil Bank’s distributable profit after regulatory adjustments rose by 13.13% to Rs. 5.63 arba. The bank’s share traded at Rs. 509 at the end of the quarter, with a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 19.60 times.

Headline: Dividend Spotlight: A Closer Look into Dividend Declarations by Companies Across All Sectors for FY 2081/82
Full Content:
A number of companies listed on the Nepal Stock Exchange Limited (NEPSE) have declared dividends for their shareholders for fiscal year 2081/82, reflecting their financial performance and commitment to investor returns. The announcements cover a broad range of sectors, with dividend distributions seen across Banking, Development Bank, Finance, Hotels and Tourism, Hydropower, Investment, Manufacturing and Processing, Microfinance, and Mutual Fund categories. These declarations include both cash and bonus shares, highlighting the varying strategies companies have adopted to reward their investors.
Meanwhile, four sectors, Life Insurance, Non-Life Insurance, Others, and Trading, have not declared any dividends this year. This contrast underscores the differing profitability levels and market conditions across industries within NEPSE. The overall dividend landscape offers valuable insights into the strength and stability of Nepal’s listed companies, serving as a key indicator for investor confidence and sectoral performance in the current fiscal period.
The following data presents a detailed breakdown of all the companies from each sector that have declared dividends this fiscal year:
Commercial Banks
The table below presents the list of commercial banks listed under the Banking Index that have declared dividends this fiscal year, along with details on bonus shares, cash dividends, AGM dates, and book closure dates.
Out of the 19 commercial banks listed under the Banking Index, only seven have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Everest Bank (EBL) declared the highest total dividend among commercial banks, distributing 20% in total, comprising 6% bonus shares and a 14% cash dividend.
Development Banks
Out of the 16 development banks listed under the Development Bank Index, only four have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Muktinath Bikas Bank (MNBBL) distributed the highest total dividend of 18.20%, including 13.53% bonus shares and a 4.67% cash dividend.
In contrast, Miteri Development Bank (MDB) declared the lowest dividend among development banks, offering only a 10% cash dividend with no bonus shares.
Finance
Only one finance company, Manjushree Finance (MFIL), has declared a dividend for FY 2081/82. The company announced a 15% cash dividend with no bonus shares.
Hotels and Tourism
From the Hotel and Tourism sector, only Soaltee Hotel (SHL) announced the total dividend of 31.5789%, comprising 15% bonus shares and a 16.5789% cash dividend.
Hydropower
Among the 94 hydropower companies listed under the Hydropower Index, only five have declared dividends for FY 2081/82. Bhagawati Hydropower Development Company (BGWT) distributed the highest total dividend of 20%, comprising 14% bonus shares and a 6% cash dividend.
At the lower end, Arun Valley Hydropower Development Company (AHPC) announced a total dividend of 8.421%, including 8% bonus shares and a 0.421% cash dividend. The overall declarations from the sector suggest selective profitability, with only a handful of hydropower companies managing to reward shareholders this fiscal year.
Investment
Out of seven companies in the sector, only Hathway Investment Nepal (HATHY) and Nepal Infrastructure Bank (NIFRA) have announced dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Hathway Investment has declared a total dividend of 12.632%, including a 12% bonus share and 0.632% cash dividend. The company’s AGM was scheduled for Bhadra 25, 2082, with the book closure date on Bhadra 13, 2082.
Nepal Infrastructure Bank has declared a 6.3158% cash dividend, without issuing bonus shares. AGM and book closure dates for NIFRA have not yet been announced.
Manufacturing and Processing
In the Manufacturing sector, only Himalayan Distillery (HDL), Nepal Lube Oil (NLO), and Unilever Nepal (UNL) have declared dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Himalayan Distillery has announced a total dividend of 25%, including a 20% bonus share and 5% cash dividend. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 30, 2082, with the book closure date on Kartik 20, 2082.
Nepal Lube Oil declared a total dividend of 21.05264%, comprising a 20% bonus share and 1.05264% cash dividend. The AGM was set for Ashwin 31, 2082, with the book closure date on Ashwin 12, 2082.
Unilever Nepal announced a cash dividend of 1842%, with no bonus shares. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 25, 2082, and the book closure period is Kartik 11–25, 2082.
Microfinance
In the Microfinance sector, only Gurans Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha (GLBSL) and RSDC Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha (RSDC) have declared dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82.
Gurans Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha has announced a total dividend of 15%, consisting of a 14.25% bonus share and 0.75% cash dividend. Its AGM is scheduled for Kartik 23, 2082, with the book closure date on Kartik 14, 2082.
RSDC Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha declared an 8% cash dividend, with no bonus shares. AGM and book closure dates for RSDC have not yet been announced.
Mutual Fund
All 52 mutual funds have declared cash dividends for the fiscal year 2081/82. Notable funds include Laxmi Unnati Kosh (20%), Sanima Large Cap Fund (21.05%), Siddhartha Equity Fund (20%), RBB Mutual Fund 1 (20%), and Sunrise Bluechip Fund (19%). Other funds have announced dividends between 5% and 20%.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Kartik Interest Rates; Machhapuchchhre Bank and NMB Bank Leads with Significant Cuts
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published new interest rates for the month of Kartik, showing a decline compared to Ashwin.
Out of the 20 commercial banks currently in operation, 14 have reduced their rates, while six banks have continued with the same rates on individual fixed deposits as in the previous month.
Machhapuchchhre Bank and NMB Bank recorded the steepest reductions, each lowering the rates on both individual and institutional fixed deposits by 1 percentage point. Headline: Nabil Bank Opens Applications for Sixth Cohort of Social Entrepreneurship Fellowship and Certificate Courses
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has announced applications for the new cohort of its Fellowship Program and Certificate Course under the Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship (Nabil SSE), aimed at fostering social entrepreneurship and inclusive development. Nepali citizens aged 18 and above can apply online until November 13, 2025 (Kartik 28, 2082).
CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali said the program aligns with national goals of poverty reduction, empowerment, and inclusive growth, focusing on marginalized communities. The six-month Fellowship Program, conducted with Tribhuvan University, offers training, mentorship, and financing support to social entrepreneurs, with 76 fellows and 62 active enterprises established so far.
The three-month Certificate Course, available in all seven provinces, has already benefited over 1,000 participants, promoting local entrepreneurship. This year, Nabil SSE will emphasize province-specific themes such as agro value chains, digital innovation, green enterprises, tourism, and rural livelihoods.
To date, Nabil SSE has contributed to over 17,000 job creations, reinforcing Nabil Bank’s commitment to sustainable development through its CSR initiatives in entrepreneurship, education, health, and climate resilience.

Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for the first month of the fiscal year 2082/83, ending in Shrawan.

The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 8.38 Arba. Nepal Investment Mega Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 63.42 Crores for the period.
Other notable performers include Rastriya Banijya Bank and Nepal Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the Agricultural Development Bank recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 37.50 lakhs.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 81.64 Crores, despite five out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Muktinath Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 15.72 Crores, outpacing Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank, which posted Rs. 13.39 Crores in net profit. Lumbini Bikas Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 11.08 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Saptakoshi Development Bank and Salapa Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 32.4 lakhs and Rs. 6.9 lakhs, respectively.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Interest Rates for Ashwin; Nine Banks Slash, Two Raise
Full Content:
Commercial banks have released their revised interest rates for the month of Ashwin, showing a slight overall decline compared to Bhadra. Out of the 20 commercial banks, nine banks maintained their rates unchanged, while 11 banks introduced adjustments. Among these, nine banks lowered their rates, whereas two banks opted for an increase.
Prime Commercial Bank, Sanima Bank, and Everest Bank have each reduced the maximum interest rate on personal term deposits by 0.5 percentage points compared to Bhadra. Citizens Bank and NIC Asia Bank followed with reductions of 0.25 percentage points, while Kumari Bank trimmed its rate by 0.2 percentage points.
Conversely, two banks raised their deposit rates for Ashwin. Laxmi Sunrise Bank increased its maximum personal term deposit rate by 0.25 percentage points, and Standard Chartered Bank made a smaller upward adjustment of 0.05 percentage points.

Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited, as the fund promoter, and Nabil Investment Banking Limited, acting as both issuer and sales manager, completed the unit allocation of the NI 31 open-ended mutual fund scheme under Nabil Mutual Fund.

Investors can check the allocation results on
iporesult.cdsc.com.np
, and further inquiries can be made via the company’s contact numbers 4511604 and 4511733.

Headline: Nabil Bank and Nimbuzz Partner to Launch eSIM and International Driving Permit Services via nBank App
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has partnered with Nimbuzz to offer international data eSIM and International Driving Permit (IDP) services through its nBank mobile app. This collaboration enables customers to purchase data plans for over 200 countries and apply for UN-standard IDPs recognized in more than 190 nations directly from the app.
The initiative aims to simplify connectivity and travel documentation for Nepali travelers, students, and migrant workers. Applications for IDPs can be completed online in under 10 minutes, with electronic permits delivered within 24 hours. Both organizations expressed confidence that the service will enhance convenience and reduce travel hassles.

Nabil Bank Limited recorded the highest net profit, earning Rs. 7.13 Arba by the end of Ashad, a 15.01% increase from the previous year. Following Nabil, Nepal Investment Mega Bank posted Rs. 6.76 Arba, while Global IME Bank earned Rs. 6.20 Arba. NIC Asia Bank recorded the lowest net profit at Rs. 16 crores, experiencing the steepest YoY decline of 77.03% from Rs. 70 crores in FY 2080/81.
Kumari Bank reported the highest profit growth among all banks, with an increase of 45,820.14%. Other banks showing notable growth after revising previous year figures include Prabhu Bank and Nepal Bank.
However, four banks—Standard Chartered Bank, Nepal SBI Bank, Citizens Bank International, and NIC Asia Bank—recorded a decline in profit during the review period, with NIC Asia Bank’s net profit falling the most.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
In terms of distributable profit per share, Everest Bank Limited (EBL) led with Rs. 38.27 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 20.47. Despite being second in total net profit, Nepal Investment Mega Bank reported the lowest distributable profit per share at Rs. 1.44. Four banks recorded negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.

Headline: Nabil Bank’s Q4 FY 2081/82 Net Profit Climbs 15.01% to Rs. 7.13 Arba on Lower Impairment Charges and Strong Deposit Growth
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL)
has published its financial results for the fourth quarter of FY 2081/82, reporting a notable improvement in profitability driven by higher operating income and reduced impairment charges.
The bank’s paid-up capital remained unchanged at Rs. 27.06 Arba, while retained earnings surged by 54.82% to Rs. 4.77 Arba. Reserves rose by 11.82% to Rs. 31.91 Arba. Deposits increased by 13.53% to Rs. 5.24 Kharba, and loans and advances to customers grew by 10.50% to Rs. 4.12 Kharba.
Net interest income was almost stable at Rs. 16.33 Arba, recording a marginal 0.06% increase. Personnel expenses rose by 12.17% to Rs. 5.23 Arba, while impairment charges dropped sharply by 48.30% to Rs. 2.40 Arba. This led to a 25.44% rise in operating profit, which reached Rs. 10.85 Arba. Net profit grew by 15.01% to Rs. 7.13 Arba.
The bank’s distributable profit after appropriation and regulatory adjustments stood at Rs. 4.77 Arba, marking a 54.82% rise. Capital adequacy declined slightly to 11.94% from 12.24%, while the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio improved to 4.27% from 4.45%. The cost of funds decreased to 4.41% from 5.86%. Earnings per share (EPS) increased to Rs. 26.34 from Rs. 22.90, and net worth per share rose by 8.63% to Rs. 235.58. At the end of the quarter, the bank’s price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio stood at 20.55 times, with a quarter-end market price of Rs. 541.37 per share.

Headline: Nabil Bank Wins Cybersecurity and Project Finance Awards at Asian Banking & Finance Awards 2025
Full Content:
Nabil Bank received two major honors at the Asian Banking & Finance Awards 2025: the ‘Cybersecurity Innovation Award – Nepal’ and ‘Nepal Domestic Project Finance Bank of the Year.’ These awards recognize the bank’s commitment to digital security and its vital role in financing Nepal’s infrastructure projects.
CEO Manoj Gyawali credited the achievements to the team’s dedication and customer trust. Nabil Bank, a pioneer in Nepal’s banking sector, continues to focus on innovation, digital transformation, and delivering advanced banking solutions through its extensive branch and ATM network.

Headline: Nabil Bank Wins Gold at NBPA 2024 for Outstanding Financial Reporting
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has won the National Best Presented Annual Report Award (NBPA) – 2024 Gold Award for the second consecutive year, presented by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN).
The award recognizes the bank’s excellence in financial transparency, corporate governance, and accountability for its 2023/24 annual report.
The report is also nominated for the SAFA BPA Awards, representing Nepal at the regional level.
With over 2.5 million customers, 268 branches, and 321 ATMs, Nabil Bank continues to lead in innovation and financial reporting excellence.

Headline: Nabil Bank Celebrates 41 Years of Excellence: Leading Nepal’s Financial Growth and Digital Innovation
Full Content:
Nabil Bank, one of Nepal’s pioneering financial institutions, has marked its 41st anniversary, highlighting a legacy of strong growth, digital leadership, and national economic contribution since its founding in 1984. Beginning with just two branches and 144 employees, the bank now serves nearly 2.5 million customers through 268 branches, 321 ATMs, and 21 extension counters.
The bank has seen exponential growth over four decades, with its net worth rising from NPR 28 million to NPR 61.24 billion, and total assets increasing from NPR 269 million to NPR 611.86 billion. Its loan and deposit volumes have also surged significantly, reinforcing its status as Nepal’s leading commercial bank.
Nabil Bank has strategically invested in productive sectors such as agriculture, energy, MSMEs, and subsidized lending, contributing to over 3,000 MW of energy generation and broad-based employment.
A trailblazer in digital banking, the bank introduced services like mobile banking, QR payments, online account opening, and online loans, making banking more accessible and efficient.
To celebrate its anniversary, Nabil launched two customer-focused initiatives: a 41-day free debit card offer for new savings accounts and the Nabil Smart Naari Home Loan Scheme, which supports women with flexible, affordable home financing and includes a lifetime free credit card.
As it moves into its 42nd year, CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali reaffirmed Nabil’s commitment to sustainable, innovative, and customer-centric banking, appreciating the stakeholders who have supported its journey.

Headline: Nabil Sustainable Banking Enters Fifth Year; ‘Nabil Green Week’ Launched to Promote Sustainability
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has announced the commencement of the fifth year of its ‘Nabil Sustainable Banking’ initiative. Marking the occasion, the bank is organizing ‘Nabil Green Week’ from June 30 to July 6 (Ashad 15 to 21), featuring various sustainability-focused programs in the presence of stakeholders from diverse sectors.
Throughout the week, a series of webinars will be held in collaboration with industry experts, including representatives from GIZ Nepal, Simple Energy Pvt. Ltd., BYD, CG Motors, and other ESG and agriculture specialists. The sessions aim to foster discussions on solar rooftop solutions, electric mobility, sustainable agriculture, and ESG-based investments, creating a platform for knowledge exchange.
Over the years, Nabil Bank has embedded sustainability into its core operations by aligning with Nepal’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The bank reports that through investments in renewable energy, it has contributed to the reduction of 11,172 tons of greenhouse gas emissions and invested in 43 hydropower projects across 21 districts. Its sustainable finance initiatives have supported over 46,000 individuals, with significant investments in agriculture, electric vehicle loans, and women-led enterprises. The bank has also emphasized digital banking, financial literacy, and inclusive growth through programs such as Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship and branchless banking services.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Baisakh; NABIL Tops the Charts Once More
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for till the tenth month of the fiscal year 2081/82, ending in Baisakh.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 47.79 Arba. Nabil Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 5.6 Arba, overtaking Global IME Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 5.35 Arba. Nepal Investment Mega Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 5.02 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Everest Bank and Nepal Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the NIC Asia Bank recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 47.87 Crores.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 4.59 Arba, despite five out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Muktinath Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 87.68 Crores, outpacing Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank which posted Rs. 86.93 Crores in net profit. Shine Resunga Development Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 61.54 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Green Development Bank and Corporate Development Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 2.32 crores and Rs. 1.56 crores, respectively.
Furthermore, eight banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Saptakoshi Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Salapa, Corporate Development Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: Prime Commercial Bank Wins Mahalaxmi Corporate Cricket League 2025 – Season 4
Full Content:
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited successfully concluded the 4th edition of the Mahalaxmi Corporate Cricket League 2025, organized on the occasion of its 31st anniversary. Held in Kathmandu from Jestha 21 to 24, 2082 (June 4–7, 2025), the tournament featured 24 teams from various banks, financial institutions, insurance companies, merchant banks, and microfinance institutions.
Prime Commercial Bank Limited clinched the championship title, while Nabil Bank Limited secured second place. The award distribution ceremony was held on Jestha 26, 2082 (June 9, 2025), where Deputy Governor of Nepal Rastra Bank, Mr. Bam Bahadur Mishra, and MLBL Chairperson Mr. Rajesh Upadhyay jointly handed over the winner’s trophy.
Individual awards were presented to:
i. Best Fielder: Amrit Chaulagain (Nabil Bank)
ii. Best Wicketkeeper: Bijay Para Limbu (Nabil Bank)
iii. Best Bowler: Anil Bartola (NMB Bank)
iv. Best Batsman & Player of the Tournament: Suraj Timilsina (ICFC Finance)
Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank expressed heartfelt gratitude to all sponsors, participating teams, and individuals who contributed to the successful execution of the tournament.

Headline: Nabil Bank Appoints Mr. Manoj Kumar Gyawali as Chief Executive Officer
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has appointed Mr. Manoj Kumar Gyawali as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Bank. The decision was made during the Bank’s 682nd Board Meeting held on 22nd Jestha, 2082.
Mr. Gyawali, who had been serving as the Acting CEO, has now been formally appointed to the position for a tenure of four years, effective from 22nd Jestha, 2082.
Mr. Gyawali had been serving as the Acting CEO prior to his official appointment. Widely recognized as a motivational speaker and an effective communicator, he brings with him over 26 years of extensive experience in the banking and capital markets sector. He is a qualified Chartered Accountant and has held significant leadership roles at Nepal Rastra Bank, Global IME Bank, Global IME Capital, and Jyoti Bikas Bank.
With his capable and visionary leadership, Nabil Bank is expected to further strengthen its financial position and achieve new milestones across key performance indicators in the days ahead.
The same board meeting also approved the promotion of Mr. Adarsha Bazgain, Deputy General Manager, to the position of Deputy Chief Executive Officer. In addition, Ms. Vishma Neupane, Chief of the Legal Department, has been entrusted with the responsibility of Company Secretary.
Nabil Bank Limited is a pioneer in Nepal’s banking sector, committed to delivering innovative and customer-centric financial solutions. With a strong focus on digital transformation, the Bank continues to redefine banking experiences across the country. Currently, Nabil Bank operates through 268 branches and a network of 320 ATMs nationwide.

Headline: Nabil Bank Wins 'The Banker’s Technology Award 2025' for Asia-Pacific
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited, one of Nepal’s leading private sector banks, has been honored with
‘The Banker’s Technology Award 2025’
for the Asia-Pacific region, recognizing its excellence in innovation, digital agility, and technological leadership. Presented by
The Banker
, a Financial Times publication, the award highlights the bank’s customer-focused digital transformation and adoption of AI, data analytics, and its nBank app.
Acting CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali stated that the award reflects the bank’s commitment to transforming the banking experience through technology. A digital pioneer since 1984, Nabil Bank introduced Nepal’s first computerized banking system and open banking model. With 268 branches and 320 ATMs nationwide, the bank continues to lead with its customer-centric, tech-driven approach to modern banking.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Fixed Deposit Rates for Jestha: NIMB Slashes, SANIMA Leads the Hike
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published their revised fixed deposit (FD) interest rates for the month of Jestha. While most banks have kept their rates unchanged compared to the previous month of Baisakh, a few have made adjustments.
Out of the 20 commercial banks, 14 banks maintained the same interest rates as in Baisakh, whereas the remaining 6 banks revised their rates, with three banks decreasing and three increasing their rates.
Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) made the steepest cut, reducing its individual fixed deposit rate by 1 percentage point, from 6.50% in Baisakh to 5.50% in Jestha.
Similarly, Siddhartha Bank Limited (SBL) lowered its rate by 0.25 percentage points, and Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) made a slight decrease of 0.01 percentage points.
Among the banks that increased individual FD rates, Sanima Bank Limited (SANIMA) led with a rise of 0.38 percentage points.
Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) followed with a 0.30 percentage point increase, while Everest Bank Limited (EBL) saw a marginal hike of 0.03 percentage points.
Additionally, Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) increased its institutional fixed deposit rate by 1 percentage point, from 3.00% to 4.00%.

Headline: Nabil Bank Expands Priority Banking Services with New Lounge at Boudha Branch
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has inaugurated its fifth Priority Banking Lounge at the Boudha branch, enhancing its premium service offerings for high-value clients. The lounge was officially opened by Deputy CEO Bhupendra Pandey and joins existing facilities at Teendhara, Lalitpur, Maharajgunj, and Kausaltar.
This expansion reflects the bank's commitment to delivering personalized, world-class banking experiences, including services like dedicated Relationship Managers, reduced wait times, and tailored financial solutions. Nabil Bank, with a network of 268 branches and 320 ATMs, continues to innovate and focus on customer-centric digital transformation.

Headline: Nabil Bank Extends Lifetime Free Credit Card Offer Until Ashadh 2082
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has extended its popular 'Nabil Lifetime Free Credit Card' scheme until Ashadh 2082 (mid-July), following high demand. The offer includes no joining, annual, or subscription fees, making credit cards more accessible and affordable.
Customers can apply online and receive the card at home. Cardholders benefit from 0% interest on Buy Now, Pay Later options and discounts at various outlets. This initiative supports the bank’s mission to provide innovative, customer-friendly, and digitally driven banking services across Nepal.

Headline: Nabil Bank Partners with Apollo Information Center to Offer Healthcare Benefits to Customers
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Apollo Information Center, the official representative of Apollo Hospital, India, to provide exclusive healthcare benefits to its customers, staff, and shareholders.
The partnership offers a 10% discount on medical services and personalized consultations at Apollo Hospital.
The initiative aims to simplify access to quality healthcare for Nepali patients traveling to India, with benefits accessible via Nabil’s digital platforms. The offer is valid for two years, reaffirming Nabil Bank’s commitment to enhancing customer value and experience.

Headline: Delving into Q3 2081/82: Performance Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks with Key Financial Insights
Full Content:
All 20 commercial banks have unveiled their financial reports for the third quarter of FY 2081/82, offering a fresh look into their performance during the nine-month period. The disclosures present a deeper understanding of their profitability, capital strength, and overall business growth. This summary captures the major highlights and evolving trends in net earnings, capital adequacy ratios, and other essential financial indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q3 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 5.05 Arba, marking an 8.21% increase over the same period last year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) followed with a net profit of Rs. 4.54 Arba, though this represents a 38.61% increase from the previous year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) took third with Rs. 4.53 Arba.
Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 2032.94% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 91.81%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.41 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 17.07 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 36.38 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 34.19 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 30.85 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 60.35 Kharba in customer deposits, with eight banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.18 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 5.02 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 4.61 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.22 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.13 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 4.01 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 77.26 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.31 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 12.32 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 12.05 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 35.07 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 5.17 Arba, with Laxmi Sunrise Bank Limited (LSL) next at Rs. 3.20 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 35.61, followed by Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) at Rs. 28.86 and Nepal Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 25.26. The industry average EPS was Rs. 15.12, with eleven banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 1.40.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 28.42 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 16.19. Six banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 332.66, followed by Agriculture Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs. 264.85 and Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 260.74. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 134.43, with the industry average at Rs. 195.92.
P/E Ratio:
Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) had the lowest P/E ratio at 9.94 times, followed by  Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at 11.92 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios, and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 17.44%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the lowest at 10.84%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.64%, while Himalayan Bank Limited (HBL) reported the highest NPL at 7.68%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 1.92% while
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported the highest
ROE at 16.10%.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 5.47%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.3%.
- CD Ratio:
Citizens Bank International Limited (CZBIL) had the highest CD ratio at 85.90%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 64.37%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 7.20%, and Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the lowest at 5.02%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.8% to 4%.
