Headline: ICRA Nepal Unleashes Rating Shake-Up: Nabil and Nepal Bank Downgraded, Chilime Reaffirmed
Full Content:
ICRA Nepal has downgraded Nabil Bank Limited’s issuer and subordinated debenture ratings while continuing its placement under ‘Watch with Negative Implications.’ The issuer rating was downgraded from [ICRANP-IR] A+@ to [ICRANP-IR] A@, and both NPR 2 billion subordinated debentures were downgraded from [ICRANP] LA+@ to [ICRANP] LA@. Despite the downgrade, the ratings still indicate an adequate level of safety and low credit risk. These ratings reflect general creditworthiness and are not investment recommendations.
Similarly, ICRA Nepal has placed Nepal Bank Limited’s issuer rating of [ICRANP-IR] A@ under ‘Watch with Negative Implications.’ This rating reflects an adequate level of safety and low credit risk in meeting financial obligations. However, the negative watch indicates potential concerns. The rating represents overall creditworthiness and is not linked to any specific debt instrument.
Also, ICRA Nepal has reaffirmed the issuer rating of [ICRANP-IR] BBB for Chilime Engineering and Services Limited, indicating a moderate level of safety in meeting financial obligations and moderate credit risk. The rating reflects the company's general creditworthiness and is not linked to any specific debt instrument.

Headline: Commercial Banks' Net Profits Rise by 1.40% in Q3; Nepal Bank Sees Over 2000% Surge, NIC Asia Suffers 91% Decline
Full Content:
Nepal's commercial banks have reported their net profits for the third quarter of the current fiscal year, according to their unaudited financial statements. The collective net profit of the 20 commercial banks stood at Rs. 41.25 Arba, marking a modest 1.40% year-on-year (YoY) growth compared to Rs. 40.68 Arba recorded during the same period in fiscal year 2080/81.
The most remarkable performance was delivered by Nepal Bank, which reported a net profit of Rs. 278.35 crores, a dramatic leap from just Rs. 13.05 crores in the same quarter last year. This translates to a staggering 2032.94% increase, making it the highest percentage growth among all commercial banks this quarter.
Strong performances were also seen from several other institutions. Nepal Investment Mega Bank posted a net profit of Rs. 454 crores, rising by 38.61% from the previous year. Similarly, Global IME Bank earned Rs. 453.41 crores, up 37.12%, while Everest Bank and Machhapuchchhre Bank posted profits of Rs. 345.76 crores and Rs. 110.26 crores, registering growths of 32.55% and 28.90% respectively.
Moderate profit growth was reported by banks like Sanima Bank (14.80%), Nabil Bank (8.21%), NMB Bank (5.87%), Prabhu Bank (3.51%), and Nepal SBI Bank (3.36%). Laxmi Sunrise Bank also posted a small increase of 2.24% in net profit.

Headline: Nabil Bank Honored as Highest Tax-Paying Bank in Nepal for FY 2079/80
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has been honored as the highest tax-paying bank by the Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FNCCI) during its 59th Annual General Meeting and Industry and Commerce Day 2081. Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli presented the certificate to Acting CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali.
The bank was recognized for its highest tax contribution in FY 2079/80 within the banking, financial, and insurance sector. Nabil Bank has received similar honors from both FNCCI and the Government of Nepal on multiple occasions. As a leading private sector bank, Nabil serves over 2.4 million customers through 268 branches and 320 ATMs, and continues to play a pioneering role in Nepal’s banking sector.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Interest Rates for Baisakh 2082; 3 Banks Cut Individual Fixed Deposit Rates, 1 Bank Hikes
Full Content:
Commercial banks have published their interest rates for the month of Baisakh 2082. Among the 20 commercial banks, 3 have reduced the maximum interest rate on individual fixed deposits, while one has increased it. The remaining 16 banks have kept their rates unchanged.
Kumari Bank, Sanima Bank, and Nepal Bank have lowered their maximum interest rates on individual fixed deposits by 0.09 percentage points, 0.1 percentage points, and 0.35 percentage points, respectively. On the other hand, Everest Bank has increased its rate by 0.61 percentage points.
In the case of institutional fixed deposits, 8 banks have lowered their maximum rates compared to Chaitra. Everest Bank stands out as the only bank that has raised its maximum interest rate for institutional fixed deposits as well.

Headline: NRB Publishes Net Profit Report for Falgun: Nabil Bank and Garima Bikas Bank Lead Their Sectors
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for the eight month of the fiscal year 2081/82, ending in Falgun.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 43.49 Arba. Nabil Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 4.78 Arba, overtaking Globel Ime Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 4.72 Arba. Nepal Investment Mega Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 4.08 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Everest Bank and Nepal Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the Agriculture Development Bank recorded the least net profit among commercial banks of Rs. 73.8 Crores.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 4.33 Arba, despite five out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Garima Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 83.48 Crores, followed by Muktinath Bikas Bank, which posted Rs. 78.78 Crores in net profit. Shine Resunga Development Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 56.48 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Green Development Bank and Salapa Bikas Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 1.8 crores and Rs. 17 lakhs, respectively.
Furthermore, eight banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Saptakoshi Development Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Corporate Development Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: Nabil Bank Launches Eco-Friendly ‘Digo Bachat Khata’ to Support Carbon Reduction and Sustainability
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has launched the Nabil Digo Bachat Khata, a savings account designed to support sustainable development and reduce carbon emissions in Nepal.
Aligned with the nation’s goal of net-zero emissions by 2045, the bank will contribute an extra 0.5% annually from total deposits in this account toward environmental initiatives such as reforestation, renewable energy, and clean water projects.
Customers maintaining a balance of Rs. 50,000 will have a tree planted in their name, and the account offers various perks, including free digital banking, debit/credit cards for the first year, and discounts on locker fees.
Aimed at individuals, NRNs, and non-profits, this innovative account blends financial benefits with environmental responsibility. Nabil Bank, serving over 2.4 million customers, reinforces its role as a leader in sustainable and modern banking in Nepal.

Headline: Nabil Bank Hosts ‘Women in Motion – Accelerate Action’ to Promote Gender Equality
Full Content:
Nabil Bank successfully organized the ‘Women in Motion – Accelerate Action’ program in Kathmandu, focusing on women empowerment, capacity building, inclusivity, and gender equality. The event was inaugurated by the bank’s independent director, Sarita Bhatta Adhikari, while Chairman Upendra Prasad Paudel reaffirmed the bank’s commitment to creating opportunities for women in the banking sector. Acting CEO Manoj Gyawali emphasized the need for increased female leadership in the industry, highlighting their role in governance and decision-making.
Nepal Super League Chairperson Ashrayata Karki Chaudhary praised Nabil Bank’s efforts in fostering workplace inclusivity and economic growth. The event featured a panel discussion titled ‘The C-Shift: Navigating Barriers and Catalyzing Leadership,’ where experts shared insights on breaking barriers for women in leadership. Nabil Bank has also been conducting various gender-focused programs, including financial literacy, workplace safety awareness, and wellness initiatives, reinforcing its commitment to gender equality in Nepal’s banking sector.

Headline: Nabil Bank Promotes Financial Literacy Nationwide Through Global Money Week 2025 Campaign
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Ltd. organized a nationwide program focusing on financial literacy across all seven provinces in Nepal as part of the "Global Money Week 2025" campaign, held from March 17 to 23. The bank targeted students and youth, aiming to raise awareness about financial matters like savings, budgeting, investment, digital literacy, and cybersecurity.
Over 4,000 students and young people participated in the program across various provinces, benefiting from financial education. Nabil Bank also runs year-round initiatives promoting financial literacy, digital banking, and social entrepreneurship, while supporting youth with concessional educational and entrepreneurial loans. Through these efforts, the bank aims to contribute to positive social change, especially in areas like entrepreneurship, education, health, disaster management, and climate change.

Headline: Nabil Bank Accepts CEO Gyanendra Prasad Dhungana’s Resignation, Appoints Manoj Kumar Gyawali as Acting CEO
Full Content:
Nabil Bank’s Board of Directors has officially accepted the resignation of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Gyanendra Prasad Dhungana. The decision was made during the bank’s 677th board meeting, held on Chaitra 13, 2081, at 8:30 AM. Dhungana tendered his resignation, effective from Chaitra 10, 2081.
In response, the board has appointed Senior Deputy CEO Manoj Kumar Gyawali as the Acting Chief Executive Officer (Acting CEO) to lead the bank’s operations.

Headline: Nabil Bank Customers Among Top Spenders in Visa Campaign, Win Travel Prizes
Full Content:
Five Nabil Bank Visa cardholders secured spots in the Best 25 Visa Spender Campaign 2081, organized by Visa International for the Dashain festival. The top 25 spenders won round-trip tickets for an international trip.
Nabil Bank honored the five winners in a special event attended by key bank officials and Visa representatives. As one of Nepal’s leading commercial banks, Nabil serves over 2.4 million customers through 268 branches and 320 ATMs, playing a crucial role in modernizing the country's banking sector over the past 40 years.

Headline: Nabil Bank Hosts Walkathon to Celebrate International Women’s Day
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited organized a walkathon across 12 locations nationwide under the theme "Women in Motion – Accelerate Action" to celebrate International Women’s Day and promote gender equality. Over 1,200 employees participated in the event, which was inaugurated at the bank’s Head Office in Teendhara by Chairman Upendra Prasad Poudyal.
CEO Gyanendra Prasad Dhungana highlighted that the bank is celebrating women's contributions throughout March with various programs. He encouraged women to take leadership roles, reaffirming the bank’s commitment to women's empowerment and inclusivity.
The initiative aimed to raise awareness, break societal stereotypes, and foster a more inclusive society. Nabil Bank, a pioneer in Nepal’s banking sector, continues to focus on innovation, digital transformation, and customer-centric financial solutions across its 268 branches and 320 ATMs.

Headline: Nabil Bank Promotes Provincial Entrepreneurship Through 'Nabil SSE Connect' Workshop in Biratnagar
Full Content:
Nabil Bank, through its Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship (Nabil SSE) initiative, successfully hosted the 'Nabil SSE Connect: Promoting Entrepreneurship Across Provinces' workshop in Biratnagar on Falgun 7. The event, held in partnership with Mahendra Morang Adarsha Multiple Campus, aimed to enhance entrepreneurship at the provincial level. Key discussions included fostering innovation, overcoming entrepreneurial challenges, and promoting local business growth.
Nabil Bank’s CEO, Gyanendra Prasad Dhungana, emphasized the program's role in creating jobs and reducing youth migration. The event featured panelists discussing the importance of entrepreneurship in provincial development, with notable contributions from government and academic leaders. Nabil SSE has already trained 543 participants, leading to the establishment of 72 businesses and creating over 1,200 jobs.

Headline: Most Commercial Banks Retain Interest Rates for Falgun; Global IME Bank Raises FD Rates
Full Content:
Commercial banks in Nepal have announced their interest rates for the month of Falgun, to be effective from Falgun 1, with most banks maintaining the same rates as in the previous month.
Global IME Bank has increased its maximum interest rates by 0.25 percentage points on both individual and institutional fixed deposit (FD) rates. Meanwhile, Citizens Bank International has reduced its institutional FD rates by 0.40%, and Laxmi Sunrise Bank has lowered its individual FD rates by 0.25%. All other commercial banks have kept their FD rates unchanged.

Headline: Nabil Bank Concludes 'Celebrating Fellowship, Journey of Impacts' Program, Welcomes Fourth Cohort of Nabil SSE
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Ltd. recently concluded the "Celebrating Fellowship, Journey of Impacts" program in Kathmandu. The program, which was conducted in collaboration with Tribhuvan University's School of Management, marked the farewell of the second and third cohorts of the Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship (Nabil SSE) fellowship and welcomed the fourth cohort. The program aims to address social challenges through entrepreneurship.
Key figures, including Prof. Dr. Mahananda Chalise and Prof. Dr. Keshar Jung Baral, emphasized the program's importance in fostering social change and promoting entrepreneurship. Nabil Bank’s Director, Nirvana Chaudhary, highlighted its role in inspiring youths to become employers despite challenges. The program has seen significant success, with 45 enterprises established by previous cohorts employing 1,200 individuals. The event also featured product exhibitions by fellows, and Nabil Bank continues to offer support for aspiring entrepreneurs through training, mentorship, and financial resources.

Headline: Nabil Bank Conducts Awareness Program on Digital Banking for Nepali Migrant Workers in Qatar
Full Content:
Nabil Bank organized an awareness program on secure digital banking for Nepali migrant workers in Qatar, titled ‘Ghar Ta Nepal’, at the Radisson Blu Hotel. Over a hundred participants attended the event and coordinated with Nabil Investment Banking and Nabil Stock Dealer Limited. The program covered topics like remittance, savings, investments, loans, and financial literacy. A special segment introduced the ‘Nabil Skilled Migrant Entrepreneurship Loan’ to support returning workers in starting businesses in Nepal.
Nepali Ambassador to Qatar, Ramesh Chandra Paudel, emphasized using formal remittance channels to safeguard money and boost Nepal’s economy. CEO Gyanendra Prasad Dhungana highlighted the crucial role of Nepali workers in Qatar and discussed online banking, loans, and investment options available through Nabil Bank. Deputy GM Adarsha Bazgain reaffirmed Nabil Bank’s commitment to empowering the Nepalese diaspora.
The event also featured NRN Association Qatar Chairman Ramesh Bhatta, who stressed financial awareness among migrants. Nabil Bank showcased its Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship (NSSE), which offers training and funding for aspiring entrepreneurs in Nepal. Mahendra Prasad Chamlagai, President of Nepal Business Association, Qatar, played a key role in coordinating the event.
Nabil Bank has long facilitated remittances for Nepali workers in Qatar, allowing instant transfers to bank accounts or collection from 20,000+ Nabil Remit agents. With 268 branches and 320 ATMs, the bank remains a leader in Nepal’s financial sector, serving over 2.4 million customers.

Headline: Performance Analysis of A-Class Banks in Q2 2081/82: Key Financial Metrics and Insights
Full Content:
The release of the second-quarter financial reports for FY 2081/82 by all 20 commercial banks sheds light on their financial performance, offering a detailed view of profitability, business volume, and key financial metrics. This analysis covers the second-quarter results, highlighting trends across net profit, capital adequacy, and other pivotal indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q2 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 3.24 Arba, marking a 1.29% increase over the same period last year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) followed with a net profit of Rs. 3.05 Arba, though this represents a 49.51% incline from the previous year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) took third with Rs. 2.83 Arba.
Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 85.50% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 92.03%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 38.12 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 10.04 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.28 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 16.41 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 35.94 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 32.02 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 29.03 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 58.91 Kharba in customer deposits, with ten banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.13 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 4.8 Kharba and Rastriya Banijya Bank (RBBL) at Rs. 4.47 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.22 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 4.07 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 3.91 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 78.17 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.27 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) leading at Rs. 8.30 Arba, closely followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 7.9 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 24.67 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 3.27 Arba, with Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) next at Rs. 2.53 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 32.67, followed by Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 32.06 and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 23.98. The industry average EPS was Rs. 14.72, with nine banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 2.03.
Distributable Profit Per Share:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 20.99 per share, followed by Sanima Bank Limited at Rs. 13.25. Six banks reported negative distributable profit per share for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 329.84, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 261.96 and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 225.79. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 133.51, with the industry average at Rs. 190.92.
P/E Ratio:
Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) had the lowest P/E ratio at 12.71 times, followed by Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) at 12.81 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 16.94%, with Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL) at 13.26%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.66%, while Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) reported the highest NPL at 6.96%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 2.16% and ROE at 16.10%. Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) followed with strong performances.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 5.69%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.38%.
- CD Ratio:
NMB Bank Limited (NMB) had the highest CD ratio at 86.76%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the lowest at 63.20%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 7.52%, and Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the lowest at 5.13%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.96% to 4%.
The table below provides a detailed overview of these financial indicators across the 20 commercial banks for Q2 FY 2081/82.
**Note: All figures are reported in Arba except for net profit, which is presented in crores for clarity.

Headline: Commercial Banks Report 4.62% Decline in Net Profit for Q2 FY 2081/82; NABIL Leads, Prabhu Bank Sees Highest Growth
Full Content:
Nepal's commercial banks have reported a decrease in net profits for the second quarter of the current fiscal year, according to their unaudited financial statements. As of the end of Poush (mid-January), the 20 commercial banks collectively earned a net profit of Rs. 27.43 Arba, marking a 4.62% drop compared to the Rs. 28.76 Arba earned during the same period last year.
Out of the 20 banks, 9 recorded a decrease in net profits, contributing to the overall decline. However, 11 banks experienced growth in their earnings. Among these, Prabhu Bank stood out with the highest increase in net profit, reporting an impressive 85.49% rise. The bank's net profit surged from Rs. 72.03 Crores last year to Rs. 133.61 Crores this year. Similarly, Nepal Investment Mega Bank saw an increase of over 57.18%, while Global IME Bank's profit grew by 49.51%, and NMB Bank's profit rose by 45.61%.
On the other hand, NIC Asia Bank experienced the steepest drop in net profit, with a staggering 92.03% decrease. The bank’s profit plummeted from Rs. 1.90 Arba last year to just Rs. 15.17 Crores this year. Kumari Bank also saw a significant decline in net profit, falling by over 68.20%, while Rastriya Banijya Bank’s profit dropped by more than 62.14%.
Nabil Bank recorded the highest net profit for the quarter, amounting to Rs. 3.24 Arba, which marks a modest 1.29% increase from the same period last year. Global IME Bank also posted a strong performance, reporting a net profit exceeding Rs. 3 Arba.
During the second quarter, 11 commercial banks surpassed the Rs. 1 Arba mark in net profits. Among them, two banks reported more than Rs. 3 Arba in net profit, while three banks earned over Rs. 2 Arba. The remaining six banks each posted profits exceeding Rs. 1 Arba. Despite the overall decline in profits, the banking sector remains an important player in Nepal's financial landscape, with some institutions continuing to demonstrate significant growth.

Headline: Nabil Bank Provides Mobile Phones to Enhance Traffic Police Operations
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has donated 20 Samsung mobile phones with Knox technology to the Kathmandu Valley Traffic Police Office as part of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative.
The handover, conducted by Senior Deputy CEO Manoj Gyawali to SSP Binod Ghimire on January 16, 2025, aims to improve operational efficiency, data security, and technology-driven service delivery in traffic management.
Knox-enabled devices will facilitate public safety applications, secure communication, and law enforcement tasks. SSP Ghimire expressed gratitude, emphasizing the enhanced effectiveness in daily duties and the potential for future collaboration with the bank.
Nabil Bank reaffirmed its commitment to societal improvement through various CSR initiatives focused on creating positive change.

Headline: Nabil Bank Conducts Free Health Camp for Raute Community in Surkhet
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited conducted a free health camp for the Raute community in Surkhet, in collaboration with HEARD Nepal and the Public Health Service Office, Surkhet, as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative.
A total of 137 people from 48 Raute families received medical check-ups, addressing health issues such as seasonal colds, pneumonia, skin diseases, and women's health concerns.
A medical team, led by Dr. Sujan Sapkota, provided health services including deworming, vitamins, and iron supplements. The camp aimed to promote health awareness and improve access to medical care while respecting the community's cultural practices.
Nabil Bank's CEO, Gyanendra Prasad Dhungana, emphasized the initiative's focus on enhancing health and sanitation. Local leaders, including Bhim Bahadur Bhandari, Chairman of Barahtal Rural Municipality, praised the bank's efforts to support marginalized communities. Nabil Bank remains committed to CSR activities that contribute to societal development.

Headline: Nabil Bank Achieves ISO 27001:2022 Certification for Information Security Management
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has been awarded the ISO 27001:2022 certification by INTERCERT, recognizing its commitment to robust information security practices and safeguarding customer data.
The certification was granted after a thorough audit of the bank’s information security management systems and controls.
CEO Gyanendra Prasad Dhungana highlighted the bank’s dedication to maintaining high-security standards and improving its information security management system.
The ISO 27001:2022 certification is an internationally recognized standard for managing and protecting sensitive information.
Nabil Bank, a pioneer in Nepal’s banking sector, continues to innovate with a strong focus on digital transformation, operating 268 branches and a network of 320 ATMs across the country.

Headline: Nabil Bank Customers to Enjoy Special Discounts at Vivanta Hotel
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has partnered with Vivanta Hotel to provide exclusive discounts to its customers. Under this agreement, Nabil Bank customers can avail up to 10% discounts on food, beverages, and spa services at Vivanta Hotel by using Nabil's debit cards, credit cards, e-banking, ATM cards, or bank transfers.
Signed by representatives from both institutions, this collaboration aims to enhance customer benefits and foster innovation in banking services. Nabil Bank, a leading commercial bank with over 2.4 million customers and a 40-year legacy, emphasizes adding value through strategic partnerships like this.

Headline: Nabil Bank Launches Toll-Free Customer Care Numbers for Enhanced Service
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has introduced toll-free numbers for its Customer Care Center, offering a cost-free and accessible communication channel for banking inquiries, support, and assistance.
This service allows customers to access a wide range of services, including account inquiries, product information, technical support, and transaction dispute resolution. Available 24/7, the toll-free numbers—16600-162245 for NTC users and 18102-162245 for Ncell users—reflect the bank's commitment to enhancing customer satisfaction and accessibility.
Key features include cost-free access, round-the-clock availability, efficient service by trained representatives, and multi-channel support through mobile apps, Viber, the website, and branch networks. Serving over 2.4 million customers via 268 branches and 320 ATMs nationwide, Nabil Bank continues to prioritize innovation and user-friendly services to enhance customer convenience.

Headline: Revised Interest Rates for Poush: NIC Asia and NMB Lead, Laxmi Sunrise Offers Lowest
Full Content:
Commercial banks in Nepal have announced revised interest rates for the month of Poush. According to the published data, while some banks have increased their rates compared to Mangsir, others have reduced them, and the majority have maintained the same rates as in the previous month.
Among the 20 commercial banks, 14 have retained their maximum interest rates on individual term deposits from Mangsir, whereas three banks have reduced these rates, and three others have implemented an increase.
NIC Asia Bank stands out as the institution offering the highest interest rate on individual fixed deposits for Poush, with a maximum rate of 6.6%. However, this represents a decline of 0.19 percentage points from the previous month. Conversely, Laxmi Sunrise Bank offers the lowest rate for such deposits, providing a maximum of 5.5% for the month of Poush.

Headline: Nabil Bank Celebrates 40th AGM with 10% Cash Dividend Endorsement, Strong Profit Growth
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited endorsed a 10 percent cash dividend at its 40th Annual General Meeting, held under the chairmanship of Upendra Prasad Paudel.
The dividend, approved after the board’s recommendation and Nepal Rastra Bank’s approval, will be distributed from the accumulated profits of the financial year 2080/81. In this year, the bank earned a net profit of 6.2 billion rupees, with significant growth in deposits (16.41%) and loans (13.65%).
The bank’s balance sheet grew by 15.76% to reach 5.07 trillion rupees. Additionally, Ananta Poudyal and Pravin Tibrewala were elected unopposed as board directors. Chairman Paudel emphasized the bank’s focus on modernization, corporate governance, and customer satisfaction.
Nabil Bank's equity growth has significantly benefited shareholders, with its market reputation remaining strong. The bank received multiple national and international awards, including recognition for being the highest taxpayer.
Nabil provides services through 268 branches and 320 ATMs, serving over 2.4 million customers. The bank also introduced NBank for digital banking and expressed gratitude to all stakeholders for their support.

Headline: Nabil Bank Launches Fourth Batch of Social Entrepreneurship Fellowship Program
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has launched the 4th batch of its fellowship program under the Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship (Nabil SSE), in collaboration with Tribhuvan University’s School of Management.
The program aims to provide knowledge and guidance to aspiring social entrepreneurs with innovative ideas. 20 participants, including 11 women, are part of this batch, engaging in eco-friendly businesses such as producing products from banana fiber, natural herbs, and candles.
The fellowship offers 18 days of action-based residential training over six months and a year of consulting services.
Nabil Bank has trained 56 social entrepreneurs through this program, with 45 successfully establishing businesses and creating employment for over 1,200 people. The program emphasizes collaboration between the university and the corporate sector for entrepreneurship development in Nepal.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Kartik; NABIL Tops the Charts Once More
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for till the fourth month of the fiscal year 2081/82, ending in Kartik.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 22.29 Arba. Nabil Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 2.69 Arba, overtaking Globel Ime Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 2.11 Arba. Nepal Investment Mega Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 1.82 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Prime Commercial Bank and Kumari Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, the Agriculture Development Bank recorded a net loss profit among commercial banks of Rs. 22.77 Crores.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 2.03 Arba, despite eight out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Muktinath Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 42.29 Crores, outpacing Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank which posted Rs. 36.84 Crores in net profit. Shine Resunga Development Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 35.43 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Jyoti Bikas Bank and Miteri Development Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 66.4 lakhs and Rs. 56 lakhs, respectively.
Furthermore, eight banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Saptakoshi Development Bank, Sindhu Bikas Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Green Development Bank, Salapa, Corporate Development Bank and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.

Headline: Nabil Bank Introduces Innovative Appointment Banking System for Time-Sensitive Customers
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has launched its Appointment Banking System to cater to busy professionals and business owners seeking efficient banking services. This system, available at the bank's Head Office in Teendhara, Kathmandu, allows customers to schedule visits for essential services like cash and cheque transactions, ensuring faster and hassle-free experiences.
Customers can book appointments easily through the Nabil Bank website or the NBank App. The service is designed to minimize waiting times and provide dedicated assistance for time-sensitive transactions.
Nabil Bank aims to enhance customer experience by embracing digital banking, offering personalized and efficient services tailored to busy individuals and businesses.
This service is currently available at the Tindhara branch, focusing on cash counter services, and aligns with Nabil Bank's vision of creating a digitally empowered, customer-focused banking ecosystem.

dividend proposed. The company has also called its 40th AGM on 27th Mangsir, 2081. The meeting will be held at Rastriya Sabha Griha, Kathmandu, starting at 10 a.m. that day.

Headline: Nabil Bank Honored as Highest Tax-Paying Bank on National Tax Day
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has once again been honored as the highest tax-paying bank in Nepal during the National Tax Day celebration. Finance Minister Bishnu Prasad Paudel presented the award at a program organized by the Internal Revenue Department, where Senior Deputy Chief Executive Officer Sujit Kumar Shakya received the certificate on behalf of the bank.
Nabil Bank has consistently received this recognition in previous years, including for fiscal years 2067/68, 2070/71, 2071/72, 2073/74, 2075/76, 2076/77, and 2077/78. As a leading financial institution in Nepal, Nabil Bank serves over 2.4 million customers through its 268 branches and 320 ATMs nationwide, contributing significantly to the country's economic and societal development.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Mangsir Interest Rates; Machhapuchchhre Bank Leads with Significant Cuts
Full Content:
Commercial banks have released their updated interest rates for Mangsir, effective from the start of the month. Among the 20 banks, 12 opted to lower their rates, seven retained the same rates as last month, and one increased its rate.
Machhapuchchhre Bank made the most notable reductions, lowering individual fixed deposit rates by 1 percent. On the other hand, Rastriya Banijya Bank stands out as the only bank to raise its rate, increasing it by 0.20 percent for individual fixed deposits.
For Mangsir, NIC Asia Bank offers the highest interest rate on individual fixed deposits, while Laxmi Sunrise Bank provides the lowest.

Headline: Nabil Bank Honored with ‘Certificate of Merit’ at SAFA Awards 2023
Full Content:
Nabil Bank received the ‘Certificate of Merit’ in the ‘Private Sector Banks’ category at the 2023 South Asian Federation of Accountants (SAFA) awards, held in Colombo, Sri Lanka, on November 11, 2024.
The SAFA Best Presented Annual Reports Award is highly regarded for recognizing excellence in financial reporting across South Asia.
This honor highlights Nabil Bank’s commitment to presenting reliable and high-quality financial statements.
The bank serves over 2.4 million customers in Nepal through 268 branches, 320 ATMs, and innovative digital banking services.

Headline: Nabil Bank Proposes 10% Cash Dividend for FY 2080/81
Full Content:

Headline: Comparative Analysis of First Quarter Reports of 20 Commercial Banks; Industry Accumulates An Average Profit of Rs. 81.16 Crores In Q1 FY 2081-82
Full Content:
The release of the first-quarter financial reports for FY 2081/82 by all 20 commercial banks sheds light on their financial performance, offering a detailed view of profitability, business volume, and key financial metrics. This analysis covers the first-quarter results, highlighting trends across net profit, capital adequacy, and other pivotal indicators.
Net Profit:
In Q1 FY 2081/82, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led with a net profit of Rs. 2.05 Arba, marking a 39.97% increase over the same period last year. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) followed with a net profit of Rs. 1.51 Arba, though this represents a 23.36% incline from the previous year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) took third with Rs. 1.46 Arba.
Siddhartha Bank Limited (SBL) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 791.46% rise, while NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) saw the largest decline at 89.06%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 36.13 Arba, followed by Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 9.43 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs. 5.43 Arba in irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all commercial banks totaled Rs. 3.46 Kharba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 17.33 Arba. Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with Rs. 37.51 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 35.03 Arba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 28.78 Arba.
Deposits From Customers:
Collectively, commercial banks gathered Rs. 58.39 Kharba in customer deposits, with nine banks surpassing this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) led at Rs. 5.12 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 4.79 Kharba and Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) at Rs. 4.33 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.13 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list in loans and advances with Rs. 3.97 Kharba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 3.81 Kharba.
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest portfolio at Rs. 81.96 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.23 Kharba, with eight banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, reflecting core banking earnings, saw Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) leading at Rs. 4.14 Arba, closely followed by Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) at Rs. 4.12 Arba.
Provisions (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 10.44 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Laxmi Sunrise Bank Limited (LSL) recorded the highest impairment charge at Rs. 1.17 Arba, with NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) next at Rs. 1.16 Arba.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) posted the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 36.57, followed by Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 34.85 and Nepal SBI Bank Limited (SBI) at Rs. 31.03. The industry average EPS was Rs. 17.47, with seven banks above this benchmark. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 2.96.
Distributable Profit:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 4.98 Arba, followed by Standard Chartered Bank Limited at Rs. 3.23 Arba. Four banks reported negative distributable profits for the quarter.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Banijaya Bank Limited (RBBL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 339.91, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 264.71 and Agricultural Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at Rs. 238.44. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 146.22, with the industry average at Rs. 196.89.
P/E Ratio:
Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) had the lowest P/E ratio at 11.2 times, followed by NMB Bank Limited (NMB) at 11.22 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 17.50%, with Agricultural Development Bank Limited (ADBL) at 13.87%. This ratio indicates a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets.
Non-Performing Loan (NPL):
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) had the lowest NPL at 0.77%, while Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) reported the highest NPL at 5.84%.
Return on Assets (ROA) & Return on Equity (ROE):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) recorded the highest ROA at 2.42% and ROE at 16.10%. Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) followed with strong performances.
Additional Indicators: Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread
- Cost of Funds:
Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) reported the highest cost of funds at 6.36%, with Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) having the lowest at 3.49%.
- CD Ratio:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RRBL) had the highest CD ratio at 97.32%, while Nepal SBI Bank Limited (SBI) had the lowest at 72.65%.
- Base Rate:
NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) had the highest base rate of 8.37%, and Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the lowest at 5.71%.
- Interest Spread:
The average net interest spread across commercial banks was around 3.95% to 4%.

Headline: Commercial Banks Report 21.63% Rise in Net Profit for Q1 FY 2081/82; NABIL Leads, SBL Shows Highest Growth
Full Content:
In the recently released financial report for the first quarter of fiscal year 2081/82, Nepal's commercial banks collectively reported a 21.63% increase in net profit, reaching Rs 16.23 Arba for the period.
Of the 20 banks, 12 recorded growth in earnings, while the remaining 8 saw a decline in net profit. Nabil Bank led the pack with the highest net profit, earning Rs 2.05 Arba, a 39.97% rise compared to the same period last year. Global IME Bank followed with a profit of Rs 1.51 Arba, while Nepal Investment Mega Bank took the third spot, securing Rs 1.46 Arba in net profit.
NIC Asia Bank posted the lowest profit, with earnings of Rs 11.05 Crores in Q1 2081/82. Meanwhile, Siddhartha Bank reported the highest improvement, with an extraordinary 791.46% surge in net profit, and Laxmi Sunrise Bank also saw significant growth, with a 420.53% rise in net profit during the review period.

Headline: NRB Report Highlights Commercial and Development Banks' Net Profits up to Bhadra; NABIL, MNBBL and ICFC Tops the Chart
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank has released the financial performance report for commercial and development banks for till the second month of the fiscal year 2081/82, ending in Bhadra.
Commercial Banks:
The collective net profit of commercial banks reached Rs. 17.69 Arba. Nabil Bank took the lead with a net profit of Rs. 1.66 Arba, overtaking Globel Ime Bank, which reported earnings of Rs. 1.56 Arba. Nepal Investment Mega Bank followed in third place, posting a net profit of Rs. 1.41 Arba for the period.
Other notable performers include Himalayan Bank and Kumari Bank, which reported profits in the higher range.
Meanwhile, Machhapuchchhre Bank recorded the lowest profit among commercial banks, earning Rs. 39.24 Crores.
Development Banks:
The development banking sector reported a total net profit of Rs. 1.64 Arba, despite six out of the 17 development banks facing losses.
Muktinath Bikas Bank led the sector, reporting a net profit of Rs. 32.58 Crores, outpacing Muktinath Bikas Bank, Shine Resunga Development Bank which posted Rs. 21.54 Crores in net profit. Garima Bikas Bank followed closely with earnings of Rs. 28.89 Crores. At the lower end of the spectrum, Salapa Bank and Corporate Development Bank recorded minimal earnings, with Rs. 48.5 lakhs and Rs. 38.8 lakhs, respectively.
Furthermore, six banks within the development banking sector, including Narayani Development Bank, Saptakoshi Development Bank, Sindhu Bikas Bank, Karnali Development Bank, Miteri Development Bank, and Excel Development Bank, reported net losses for the month.
Finance
Despite facing losses reported by four out of the 17 companies in this category, the finance sector in Nepal recorded a net profit of Rs. 36.43 Crores. ICFC Finance showcased remarkable performance, reporting an impressive net profit ofRs. 8.57 crore. Progressive Finance closely followed with earnings of Rs. 8.17 crore.
On the flip side, Capital Merchant Banking & Finance, NSML, Best Finance Company, and Samriddhi Finance Company faced challenges as they grappled with net losses during the same period.

Headline: Commercial Banks Unveil Kartik Interest Rate Adjustments: SANIMA Raises Rates While CZBIL and HBL Implements Significant Cut
Full Content:

Headline: Nabil Bank and Smart Ideas Pvt Ltd Join Forces for Card-Based Remittance Services
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited and Smart Ideas Pvt Ltd (Hamro Patro) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to launch card-based remittance services.
The agreement allows users of Hamro Patro's calendar app, particularly those outside Nepal, to send remittances by accessing the 'Remittance' feature in the app.
Users can send between $100 and $5,000 using international MasterCard or Visa cards, with recipients in Nepal receiving funds immediately in any bank account.
Nabil Bank has offered the nRemit service through the nBank app since December 2022, and this collaboration marks the first open banking initiative in Nepal, as stated by Adarsha Bazgain, Deputy General Manager of International Business at Nabil Bank.
Both organizations aim to streamline remittance, strengthening the Nepali banking sector.
Nabil Bank has been a key player in Nepal's banking industry for 40 years, serving over 2.4 million customers through its extensive branch and ATM network.

Headline: Commercial Banks Revise Ashwin Interest Rates; NMB Bank Leads with Significant Cuts
Full Content:
Commercial banks in Nepal have published their revised interest rate notices for the month of Ashwin, effective from Ashwin 1. The new rates reveal a combination of reductions and increases across various banks.
Out of the 20 commercial banks currently operating, nine have decreased their interest rates for individual fixed deposits, while two have implemented increases. The remaining nine banks have maintained their interest rates from the previous month, Bhadra.

In contrast, Agriculture Development Bank and Nepal Bank Limited have increased their rates for individual fixed deposits.

On the other end, Sanima Bank is providing the lowest rate at 5.90% for individual fixed deposits. Institutional fixed deposits also show significant variation, with NIC Asia Bank offering a maximum rate of 6.18%, while Sanima Bank’s rate stands at 4.30%.

Headline: Commercial Banks Reduce Base Interest Rates to 7.92% Amid Surplus Loanable Funds
Full Content:
Commercial banks in Nepal have reduced their average base interest rate to 7.92% for the period between mid-August and mid-September, driven by an excess of loanable funds. This marks a 0.25 percentage point decrease compared to the previous months, signaling a potential reduction in lending rates in the near future.
According to reports from the 20 commercial banks, Standard Chartered Bank has set the lowest base rate at 6.22%, followed by state-owned Rastriya Banijya Bank with a rate of 6.66%. On the higher end, NIC Asia Bank maintains the highest base rate at 9.22%, while Kumari Bank follows closely with 8.90%.
Over the past few months, banks have been gradually lowering their interest rates, with the average base rate consistently remaining in single digits since May 2024.
The lending rate of a bank is determined by adding a premium to its base rate, which typically ranges from 1.5% to 5%, depending on the nature of the loan and associated risks.
The reduction in base rates comes amid an economic slowdown, rising non-performing assets (NPAs), and challenges related to capital adequacy ratios. However, banks have shown improvement in key areas, including increased lending for auto loans and loans secured against shares as collateral. Records from Nepal Rastra Bank also reveal that banks have reduced a portion of their NPAs while strengthening their capital adequacy positions.
As lending rates are likely to follow the downward trend in base rates, businesses and individuals may benefit from more affordable loan opportunities in the coming months.

Headline: Nabil Bank Successfully Passes Special Resolutions for Issuance of Non-cumulative Preference Shares
Full Content:
Nabil Bank's special general meeting, chaired by Upendra Prasad Paudel, approved the issuance of Rs. 5 Arba worth of Irredeemable Non-cumulative Preference Shares.
This decision aims to bolster the bank’s capital base to support business growth and manage risks.
The shares, which do not carry voting rights, will be offered to institutional investors and are a first for the Nepalese market.
Paudel expressed gratitude for the support from stakeholders and highlighted the bank's commitment to modernizing Nepal's banking sector, enhancing commercial and industrial activities, and contributing to the country's economy and social responsibilities. Nabil Bank, with 268 branches and 316 ATMs, continues to prioritize digital banking and customer satisfaction.

Headline: Nabil Bank Unveils Special Auto Loan Scheme for NADA Auto Show 2024
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited has launched a special auto loan scheme targeting the upcoming Nada Auto Show 2024, scheduled from Bhadra 11th to 17th at Bhrikutimandap in Kathmandu.
The bank is offering attractive fixed interest rates of 8.25% for 5 years and 8.49% for 7 years to facilitate long-term auto financing.
A dedicated service booth will be available at the NADA show, where customers can receive immediate loan offer letters after selecting a vehicle. Nabil Bank has also introduced various other offers to enhance customer experience during the festive season.
As one of Nepal's leading commercial banks, Nabil Bank continues to play a significant role in the country's banking sector, serving over 2.4 million customers through its extensive network of branches and ATMs.

Headline: Nabil Bank Limited Calls SGM on September 2; When's the Book Closure Date?
Full Content:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) has called its Special General Meeting (SGM) on September 2, 2024. The 662nd meeting of the board of directors held on August 11, 2024, decided to call SGM and declared book closure from August 23, 2024. Thus, the shareholders maintained till that day are eligible to attend this meeting.
The key agenda for the SGM includes the issuance of "Nabil's 8% Irredeemable Non-cumulative Preference Shares" and the proposal to increase the bank's authorized, issued, and paid-up capital. Additionally, necessary amendments to the bank's regulations will be deliberated upon during the meeting.
This SGM is crucial for shareholders, as it will determine the future financial and operational strategies of Nabil Bank. Shareholders are encouraged to participate actively in the discussions and decisions that will shape the bank's path forward.

Headline: Nabil Bank Invites Applications for Fourth Batch of Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has announced the fourth batch of its Nabil School of Social Entrepreneurship program for 2024, following the success of the previous batch.
The program is open to Nepali citizens over 18 years old with innovative ideas for social change across sectors such as agriculture, tourism, energy, environmental protection, and IT.
The six-month program, conducted in collaboration with Tribhuvan University's School of Management, offers free training and mentorship for aspiring entrepreneurs.
So far, 56 social entrepreneurs have been trained, with 80% establishing enterprises and creating over 1,184 jobs. The bank believes this program will help participants achieve long-term success and contribute to strengthening the local economy.

Headline: Nabil Bank Partners with Namaste Pay Wallet to Enhance Digital Services
Full Content:
Nabil Bank has partnered with Namaste Pay Wallet, allowing Nabil Bank customers to use Namaste Pay Wallet services. The partnership was formalized with a memorandum of understanding signed by Niraj Sharma, Head of Retail Transaction Banking at Nabil Bank, and Vinay Bijukchhe, Deputy CEO of Namaste Pay Wallet.
This collaboration enables Nabil Bank customers to load money into their Namaste Pay Wallet and transfer funds between their wallet and bank account via the nBank (Mobile Banking) app.

Additionally, Nabil NBank app users will gain access to services from e-sewa, Khalti, and Namaste Pay Wallet, making digital payments more convenient and secure. Nabil Bank, a prominent commercial bank in Nepal, serves over 2.4 million customers through 268 branches and 316 ATMs and has been a significant contributor to the country's banking sector for 40 years.

Headline: Unveiling Q4 2080/81: A Comprehensive Analysis of Leading Commercial Banks and Key Financial Insights
Full Content:
The release of the fourth-quarter financial reports for the fiscal year 2080/81 by all 20 commercial banks offers an in-depth perspective on their financial performance, in adherence to mandatory disclosure requirements. This analysis focuses on the profitability and business volume indicators of commercial banks during this period, highlighting the nuances of these pivotal metrics. Let us delve into a comprehensive examination of the data.
Net profit:
In the fourth quarter of FY 2080/81, Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led the net profit rankings, earning Rs. 7.06 Arba, reflecting a 10.23% increase compared to the same period last year.
Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) secured the second position with a net profit of Rs. 6.02 Arba, although this marked a 10.13% decline from the previous year. Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) followed in third place with a net profit of Rs. 5.2 Arba.
Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) stood out with the highest growth, achieving a staggering 1499.04% increase in net profit. In contrast, NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) experienced the most significant decline, with a 68.91% drop in net profit for the quarter.
Paid-up capital:
The bank with the highest paid-up capital is Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) with Rs 36.13 Arba capital, Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) with Rs. 34.13 Arba, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 27.06 Arba paid-up capital. Meanwhile, Standard Chartered Bank Nepal (SCB) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 9.43 Arba.
Note: ADBL Capital includes Rs 5.43 Arba irredeemable non-cumulative preference shares.
Reserve and surplus:
The collective reserve and surplus of all commercial banks stood at Rs. 3.28 Kharba, with the industry average being Rs. 16.44 Arba. Rastriya Banijaya Bank Limited (RBBL) led with a reserve and surplus of Rs. 37.36 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) at Rs. 32.51 Arba, and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) at Rs. 27.13 Arba.
Deposits from Customers:
Commercial banks collectively amassed Rs. 2.83 Kharba in customer deposits on average. Nine banks surpassed this average. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) topped the list with Rs. 4.87 Kharba in deposits, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 4.62 Kharba, and Nepal Investment Mega Bank (NIMB) with Rs. 4.29 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the lowest deposit collection at Rs. 1.12 Kharba.
Loans and advances to Customers:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) led in loans and advances, disbursing Rs. 3.73 Kharba. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) followed closely with Rs. 3.69 Kharba. Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) had the smallest loan and advances portfolio at Rs. 81.14 Arba. The industry average loan disbursement was Rs. 2.17 Kharba, with nine commercial banks exceeding this average.
Net Interest Income:
Net interest income, the net earnings from core banking activities, saw Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) at the top with Rs. 16.64 Arba, followed by Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) with Rs. 16.21 Arba.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks allocated Rs. 36.96 Arba for loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments. Global IME Bank Limited (GBIME) had the highest impairment charge at Rs. 3.74 Arba, followed by Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) at Rs. 3.56 Arba.
Major indicators:
Earnings per share:
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) provided the highest annualized EPS at Rs. 35.09 per share. Everest Bank Limited (EBL) followed with Rs. 31.45 per share, and Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) came in third at Rs. 26.09 per share. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 8.80 per share. The industry average EPS stood at Rs. 17.80, with nine banks exceeding this average.
Distributable Profit:
Nabil Bank Limited (NABIL) reported a distributable profit exceeding Rs. 3.86 Arba, while Everest Bank reported Rs. 3.51 Arba. Conversely, four commercial banks reported negative distributable profits.
Net worth per share:
Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) had the highest net worth per share at Rs. 338.94, followed by Nepal Bank Limited (NBL) at Rs. 257.57, and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) at Rs. 236.06. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) had the lowest net worth at Rs. 141.47 per share. The industry average net worth was Rs. 192.91 per share, with eight banks exceeding this average.
P/E Ratio:
Prabhu Bank Limited (PRVU) had the lowest PE ratio at 8.6 times, followed by Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) at 11.40 times. These PE ratios reflect the quarter-end values, and recent market prices should be considered for current ratios.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) reported the highest CAR at 17.16%, followed by Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL) at 13.83%. The CAR measures a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Non-Performing Loan:
Everest Bank Limited (EBL) reported the lowest NPL at 0.71%. Kumari Bank Limited (KBL) and Nepal Investment Mega Bank Limited (NIMB) had the highest NPL at 4.95%.
Return on Asset & Return on Equity
Return on Asset (ROA): ROA is a financial metric that measures a company's efficiency in generating profit from its assets. It indicates how effectively a company utilizes its assets to generate earnings. It is calculated by dividing the net income by the average total assets.
Return on Equity (ROE): ROE is a financial ratio that measures the profitability of a company in relation to its shareholders' equity. It shows how much profit a company generates with the money shareholders have invested. ROE is calculated by dividing net income by shareholders' equity.
In the fourth quarter, Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) emerged as the frontrunner among commercial banks, boasting an impressive Return on Asset (ROA) of 2.35% and Return on Equity (ROE) of 16.09%. Following closely behind, Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) exhibited a strong performance with an ROA of 1.40%, and Everest Bank Limited (EBL) with an ROE of 13.32%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, NMB Bank Limited (NMB) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.31%, whereas Standard Chartered Bank Limited (SCB) has the lowest cost of funds at 3.84%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Likewise, Prime Commercial Bank Limited (PCBL) has reported the highest CD ratio of 86.20%, whereas Rastriya Banijya Bank Limited (RBBL) has the lowest CD ratio of 60.82%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which Commercial banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. NIC Asia Bank Limited (NICA) reports the highest base rate of 9.19%, and Standard Chartered Bank Nepal Limited (SCB) has the lowest base rate of 6.60%.
Similarly, the net interest rate spread is the difference between the interest rate a bank pays to depositors and the interest rate it receives from loans to consumers. Here, the commercial banks have net interest rate spread hovering around 3.95%- 4%

Headline: 20 Commercial Banks Report Q4 FY 2080/81 Results: Nabil Bank Tops Profit Charts with Rs 7.06 Arba, Industry Total Hits Rs 64.15 Arba

Among these banks, 10 reported an increase in earnings for Q4 2080/81, while the remaining 10 experienced a decline in net profit. Kumari Bank's net profit rose by 345.67%, Prime Commercial Bank's by 267.19%, and Agriculture Development Bank's by 176.23%.
